## Body

ROUND 1 performance verdict: PASS-WITH-NOTES.
Subject: pr:314
Head: 2ad9e18ca43c1b55fed3b44d962303d9e75f31e6

No demonstrated normal-use cost breach blocks this head. Maintenance adds no process-launch site, subscriber, poll, or timer. The queue recovery is one atomic write transaction, and failed holds remain outside both claim preflight and next-due timer selection. The PR's Cost table nevertheless understates complete renewal/sweep work and overstates its 64-row storage bound. Record the following non-blocking cost notes; this verdict does not clear another role's findings.

Verified cost model:

| Path | Trigger/rate | Actual scaling |
|---|---|---|
| Normal heartbeat | Existing heartbeat cadence | One additional in-memory lapse-membership check; recovery only on a told lapse, with retry on a later heartbeat after failure. |
| Queue recovery | Renewal edge | Schema-version read, one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, recipient-failed-row SELECT, one guarded UPDATE per selected hold, payload decoding, COMMIT. |
| Complete renewal | Renewal edge | In addition to the queue transaction: one separately committed delivery.outcome per recovered body and the renewed-edge publication. Native lock stays held across this work. Each outcome also broadcasts to existing subscribers. |
| Held send | Per send while lapsed | Schema/read for count over recipient failed history; enqueue transaction; existing head-parking loop and parking/event commits; receipt publication. Parking can process a pre-existing backlog, not only the new body. |
| Park follower | Existing live events; sweep 60 seconds after completion, 30 seconds after failure; immediate sweep after observed subscriber drop | Newly examines held parks in the existing 24-hour event window. Cost follows parks in that window, not just currently held rows. Adds recipient lookup before deadline, and an expiry eligibility attempt after deadline; existing audit, admission, FYI-page and notice-transport work remains. |
| Claims/timers | Existing claim/event-driven wait | jobs_claimable(state, kind, id) isolates pending/running rows. Failed holds contribute no claim candidates or next-due deadlines; no not_before index is needed for that isolation. |
| Storage/memory | Message admission and renewal | Two hours bounds automatic recovery eligibility, not deletion of the jobs row. Recovery retains all returned Job payloads until outcome publication finishes; memory follows their total payload bytes. |

Non-blocking notes:

1. Successful recovery still causes repeated expiry work. At the original deadline, notify_one finds no expiry notice to audit/admit; expire_native_hold returns false for the recovered/delivered row, and no terminal "not owed" fact is recorded. Every later sweep revisits it until the park leaves the 24-hour lookback. Each revisit includes a native-lock acquisition and queue write transaction, besides audit/admission/FYI reads. A two-hour hold recovered early can therefore cause roughly 22 hours of these unnecessary once-per-sweep checks. Existing retry machinery need not be replaced: a focused follow-up can preserve the negative terminal decision. Source: crates/daemon/src/park_notice.rs:301-333,459-510; crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:980-982; crates/store/src/queue.rs:847-880.

2. "Renewal: one transaction" is true of Queue::recover_held_native_deliveries, not the entire renewal edge. With H successfully recovered bodies, its queue transaction is followed by H outcome commits plus the renewed-edge commit, under the global native lock. Source: crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:457-508,955-971,2840-2881; crates/daemon/src/events/mod.rs:78-94; crates/store/src/spine.rs:267-275.

3. Sixty-four is a held-send admission brake, not a hard total-row ceiling. park_native_receiver parks the entire eligible pre-existing backlog without that check. An exact-source SQL probe parked 65 previously queued bodies and counted 65 current holds. Expired failed rows are also retained. Price renewal and sweep using actual H and 24-hour park-event volume; do not claim all storage is <=64 rows aged <=2 hours. Source: crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:840-890,912-935; crates/store/src/queue.rs:891-950.

4. Indexed does not mean history-independent. held count/selection uses jobs_serial(serial_key,state) but evaluates deadline/outcome against all failed rows for that recipient. Recovery's inherited duplicate guard filters only live state, msg_id and origin, without kind/recipient, so its candidate walk includes global live jobs. Python SQLite 3.54.1, all 48 forward migrations, exact SQL extracted from this head: selecting 64 holds rose from 1,012 to 26,974 VM instructions with 2,000 expired recipient rows; count rose from 1,617 to 27,617. Recovering 64 rows rose from 28,961 to 1,180,960 VM instructions with 2,000 unrelated live jobs. Claim preflight remained 55 instructions with either 64 or 2,064 failed rows. These are synthetic query-work receipts, not measured daemon CPU or live SQLx timings. Source: crates/store/src/queue.rs:775-844,327-357; migrations/0002_queue.sql:39-40 and migrations/0028_message_origin.sql:10-12.

Policy/brakes: delayed delivery and its two-hour eligibility window are POLICY. The held-send cap, legacy not_before=0 exclusion, and unchanged receiver-live claim guard are BRAKES: removing them permits more admission/recovery/delivery. Expiry is a policy terminalization, not an age-based row deletion.
